body:
> Found operating this board on 2026-09-02, landing track #217's stacked node PRs bottom-up. #260 and #261 both
> merged into `kb/259` and immediately went invisible: both sit in *review* with `prs: []`, their work landed,
> and nothing on the board able to say so.

## Why

#234 fixed the case where GitHub will not link a PR: `openPrsByHead` (`src/tasks.js`) lists the repo's **open**
PRs and matches them by head branch, so a card whose PR targets a non-default base is still associated with it.
That is what stopped #227 and #228 from vanishing.

The fallback is scoped to *open* PRs, and that is where it ends. The moment a stacked PR **merges**, it leaves
that listing, GitHub still refuses to link it (the base was never the default branch, and merging does not
change that), and the card is back where #227 started — except now the work is genuinely landed, so nothing is
wrong except the board's account of it:

```
#259  review  state:OPEN  prs:[264]   ← its PR targets main, still open
#260  review  state:OPEN  prs:[]      ← PR267 merged into kb/259
#261  review  state:OPEN  prs:[]      ← PR269 merged into kb/259
```

`hkb merge 260` had already run and recorded its review on the card. The merge succeeded. The card still cannot
be moved off *review* by anything the board does, because `reconcileClosed` reasons about issues GitHub closed
and the `active_pr` guard reasons about open PRs — and this card is neither.

`checkOrphanedPrs` (#234's other half) does not catch it either: it looks for an **open** PR on an hkb branch
whose card is closed. This is the mirror image — a **merged** PR whose card is open — and nothing looks for it.

This is not hypothetical tidiness. A card stuck in *review* holds its slot in every count an operator reads, and
the one thing the board exists to answer — what is actually finished — is wrong.

## What

- **Match merged PRs too, not only open ones.** The head-branch fallback should consider a recently merged PR on
  a branch this card owns (`taskBranchRe`) as that card's PR, carrying `merged: true`. One listing with
  `state=all` bounded by a recent window, or the same listing already made plus a targeted lookup — the budget
  matters, so pick deliberately and say which in the PR.
- **A card in *review* whose PR merged should reach *done*.** That is the whole point of the association: the
  tick already moves a card whose PR merged; it simply never sees this one. Decide whether that lands in
  `reconcileClosed` or in the review pass, and make it work whatever base the PR targeted.
- **`hkb doctor` gains the mirror check.** `checkOrphanedPrs` finds an open PR whose card is closed; this is a
  merged PR whose card is open. Same shape, opposite polarity, and the same cheap listing answers both.
- **Say what a non-default base costs**, once, where a track author will read it: a PR that does not target the
  default branch is invisible to GitHub's issue linkage forever, not just while it is open. #245's track-branch
  model makes this the *normal* case rather than an accident, so it has to work rather than be worked around.

## Done when

- [ ] A card whose PR merged into a non-default branch is still associated with that PR, with a test using a
      merged PR on a `kb/<n>` head.
- [ ] Such a card reaches *done* rather than sitting in *review* forever.
- [ ] `hkb doctor` flags a merged PR on an hkb branch whose card is still open.
- [ ] The extra reads are bounded and the choice is stated in the PR.
- [ ] `npm run lint && npm test` pass; the review-loop wiki page covers both polarities.
goal: A card whose PR merged into a non-default branch is still associated with it and reaches done rather than sitting in review; doctor flags a merged PR on an hkb branch whose card is open; the extra reads are bounded and the choice stated
title: A card whose PR merged into a non-default branch goes invisible again: the head-branch fallback covers open PRs only
